layout: 2×2 row major, 4 independently painted poses per age, independent generation calls
prompts:
Make one square 2-by-2 character animation model sheet, each quadrant a single completely isolated full body sprite. Exactly 4 drawings, all the same character facing LEFT in strict side profile, taking FOUR successive phases of one ordinary four-beat walking cycle. Image 1 is the sole identity/age/style reference, a game catalogue still of this particular dog. Keep the original low-resolution earthy pixel clusters, mauve-brown dark outline, warm grey / bluish smoky merle patches in exactly the same positions, solid warm cream chest and muzzle, near shoulder patch, beige small eyebrows, giant upright pointed corgi ears with peach lining, small dark eye with glint, and same little fluffy white-tipped tail. Same head, body length, height, coat markings and evenly spaced framing across all four drawings. Draw a useful game animation, not a montage of looking around. Leftward walking means forward is LEFT. Lift the near legs and pass silhouettes clearly apart; two far legs in darker shadow, two close legs in light. On all four drawings make all four short feet easy to distinguish with negative space. Show clearly changed fore- and hind-leg angles, bent joints, and changes in foot contact. Realistic walking at least one paw grounded continuously. No bounding or airtime. No repeated standing pose, copied leg positions, change of viewpoint, big smiling face or tongue out. Arrange on two rows: upper-left is contact one: near foreleg extends FAR LEFT planted forward, far foreleg trails behind and near rear leg stretches behind to RIGHT while far rear reaches forward; upper-right is passing phase: near foreleg is vertical under the chest supporting, far forepaw curls up sweeping forward and near hind paw is lifted curling under belly; lower-left is OPPOSITE CONTACT: flat far foreleg stretched out left leading, light near foreleg trails right behind chest, near rear paw reaches forward left under belly to plant, far rear trails; lower-right is opposite passing: far foreleg vertical carries chest, light near forepaw distinctly bent and raised to swing forward with a clear gap under its toes, near hindleg pushes off behind and far hind paw passes. Keep body steady while the articulated paw silhouettes change; don't rotate the full sprite. Center dogs independently, nose-left, ears upright, ample transparent clearance from edges, all paws atop one invisible ground line in each quadrant. Pixel art at roughly 70-80 game pixels per body, chocolate outline and modest highlights from the supplied pixel sprite; bold readable deliberate pixel shapes after downsampling. No frame lines, captions, labels, ground, objects, motion lines, shadows, glow or background. Transparent canvas.
The adult is a mature female Welsh Corgi, with her reference's longer long-low torso, stocky rear, tapered narrow muzzle and well-defined hocks on stubby legs. Use her blue-merle pattern and the large cream ruff, cream forehead blaze and dark patch at the eye exactly like adult reference. Draw fore and hind leg extensions deliberately on this long adult silhouette.

The puppy is the juvenile female Welsh Corgi in this one puppy reference, rounded large head nearly the depth of the chest, oversized ears, compact squat body, broad light cream muzzle, very short baby legs, tiny fluffy white tail. Match the puppy's coat and head/body ratio, not adult proportions. Each pose is independently storyboarded as a puppy's lively short-stepped grounded walk: bold little paws, generous gaps between toes in the passing poses, a tightly folded raised forepaw, changes in weight, slight natural puppy bob. No chibi embellishments, do keep recognisable catalogue pixel anatomy.
